text.text: Multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) enables simultaneous biomarker profiling, yet unmixing colocalized targets with identical spectra, such as dual-DAB marking Tau and Amyloid-β in Alzheimer's pathology, remains mathematically ill-posed.
We propose MorphoStain, an unsupervised, physics-guided framework for morphological stain decomposition with epistemic uncertainty quantification.
MorphoStain models stain separation via a conditional Latent Diffusion Teacher operating on a Beer-Lambert optical-density manifold, guided by pathology foundation models.

To enable real-time clinical throughput, the teacher is distilled into a FastStudentU-Net (0.12M parameters, > 1,400× compression), while a Symmetric Morphological Routing Module dynamically disentangles identical chromogen overlap.
text.formatted: To enable real-time clinical throughput, the teacher is distilled into a FastStudentU-Net (0.12M parameters, > 1,400× compression), while a Symmetric Morphological Routing Module dynamically disentangles identical chromogen overlap.

text.text: Evaluated on 9,908 held-out patches from the SEA-AD cohort, MorphoStain achieves 40.56 dB PSNR and 0.9961 SSIM at 140.1 FPS, showing statistically significant gains over InverseAE (Cohen's d = 3.52) and NMF (Cohen's d = 7.02), with p < 0.001 for both comparisons.

text.text: M ULTIPLEX immunohistochemistry (mIHC) visualizes multiple molecular biomarkers within a single tissue section using distinct chromogens, enabling spatially resolved profiling with standard brightfield RGB scanners [1]- [4].
text.formatted: M ULTIPLEX immunohistochemistry (mIHC) visualizes multiple molecular biomarkers within a single tissue section using distinct chromogens, enabling spatially resolved profiling with standard brightfield RGB scanners <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">[1]</ref>- <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">[4]</ref>.

text.text: In Alzheimer's disease (AD), co-staining amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau captures interacting pathologies, making accurate computational stain unmixing essential for downstream quantification.

However, because plaques and neuritic structures are fine, weakly stained, and spatially adjacent, standard RGB sensors face a fundamental physical limit: under the Beer-Lambert model, optical density (OD) is a linear combination of stain absorption vectors [5], making the inversion of m > 2 overlapping stains ill-conditioned or strictly underdetermined.

text.text: Beyond this loss of identifiability, severe spectral crosstalk amplifies ambiguity.
Precipitates like 3,3'-diaminobenzidine (DAB, brown) vary strongly in intensity and approach black at saturation, competing with the hematoxylin (blue) counterstain.
Consequently, pixel-wise color matching [5]- [7] often misassigns signals or fragments fine structures.

text.text: Resolving overlapping chromogens requires spatial morphology and learned priors (Fig. 1).

text.text: While supervised deep models [8], [9] learn spatial context, they require costly annotations.

text.text: Unsupervised methods like InverseAE [10]- [12] avoid annotations but remain deterministic, yielding a single point estimate without quantifying decomposition ambiguity across weakly stained plaques.

text.text: Conversely, diffusion models [13]- [15] can model multi-modal posteriors and provide uncertainty estimates, but deploying them across gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) incurs prohibitive latency, and uncalibrated stochastic sampling may violate physical image-formation constraints.

text.text: To bridge this gap, we introduce MorphoStain, a physicsguided latent diffusion teacher paired with a compact distilled student for uncertainty-aware Aβ/tau stain unmixing.

Our contributions are fourfold: • Physics-Guided Latent Diffusion Teacher: We combine a calibrated Beer-Lambert projection (S AD ∈ R 3×2 ) with a latent diffusion model conditioned on the Phikon pathology foundation model [16], using Monte Carlo sampling to estimate calibrated epistemic uncertainty (u var ).

text.text: • Lightweight Student: Through knowledge distillation with dilated residual blocks (d ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} [17]- [19]), we achieve a > 1,400× compression (169.67M → 0.12M parameters) for real-time WSI inference.

text.text: • Symmetric Morphological Routing (M attn ): A dedicated attention module that disentangles Aβ and tau morphologies, suppresses bleed-through, and preserves fine neuritic structures.

• Comprehensive Benchmarking: Extensive evaluation across 9,908 test patches, including zero-shot out-ofdistribution (OOD) generalization and scanner illumination shifts [20], demonstrating promising reconstruction fidelity [21]- [23], morphological preservation, and uncertainty calibration.

text.text: Classical unmixing operates in OD space via the Beer-Lambert law.
Early methods rely on fixed OD vectors [5], singular value decomposition (SVD)-based plane estimation [6], or unsupervised matrix factorization [7], [24]- [26].

text.text: Classical color deconvolution methods [5], [6] suffer from severe crosstalk bleed when resolving spectrally identical chromogens, whereas unconstrained generative models [11] drift into ill-posed solutions without physical priors (Table II).

text.text: MorphoStain bridges this gap by anchoring a Latent Diffusion Teacher within a Beer-Lambert OD manifold.

By fixing the distilled student's objectives to the analytical Moore-Penrose projection, it preserves exact spectral conservation and bypasses the high-frequency sampling variance inherent in iterative stochastic diffusion.
Furthermore, resolving dual-DAB mIHC in Alzheimer's pathology [1] typically forces standard matrix factorization into a single uninformative channel.

text.text: Our Symmetric Morphological Routing Module (M attn ) circumvents this by leveraging slide-level cohort metadata as a weakly supervised prior, enabling zero-shot, label-free biomarker separation.

Finally, the epistemic uncertainty head (u var ) provides an automated clinical safety gate; as shown in Fig. 5, predicted variance closely tracks local reconstruction error (ECE = 0.0125) to flag out-of-focus and boundary artifacts without human intervention.

text.text: Despite strong generalization across external cohorts, three operational limitations motivate future work: 1) Static Calibration: Extreme over-staining may violate nominal OD bounds.

3) Multiplexing Scope: Currently targeting M = 2, extending M attn to softmax-gated multi-head decoders for higher-order multiplex immunofluorescence (M ≥ 4) remains an important direction.

MorphoStain introduces a physics-guided teacher-student framework that unifies Beer-Lambert constraints with pathology foundation models and latent diffusion to resolve the mathematically ill-posed stain decomposition problem.

By distilling diffusion priors into a lightweight student anchored by morphological routing, the framework achieves SOTA realtime inference, separates overlapping identical chromogens without pixel-level annotations, and provides calibrated epistemic uncertainty for automated quality control.

Extensive evaluations demonstrate significant statistical gains, zero-shot domain transferability, and robust resilience to optical shifts, establishing MorphoStain as a scalable and reliable tool for quantitative clinical neuropathology.

This study exclusively utilized publicly available, deidentified human neuropathological and breast cancer immunohistochemical whole-slide imaging datasets obtained from the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) Data Portal and the Breast Cancer Immunohistochemical Image Generation (BCI) Challenge.

Because no new human subjects were recruited and no identifiable patient information was accessed, this secondary computational analysis was exempt from additional IRB approval.

(A) Beer-Lambert Physics Module: Converts input patches I RGB ∈ R 3×512×512 to optical density (OD) space Y = -log 10 (clamp(I RGB , ϵ, 1.0)) to derive initial physical concentrations C pinv = S pinv • Y ∈ R²×512×512 via analytical Moore-Penrose projection using calibrated absorbance matrix S AD .

(B) Physics-Guided Teacher Diffusion (Offline Stage): Operates on downsampled concentration priors c0 = Interp(C pinv ) ∈ R B×2×64×64 alongside variational autoencoder (VAE) spatial latents Z lat ∈ R B×4×64×64 conditioned on frozen Phikon pathology vision transformer (ViT) embeddings Z cond ∈ R B×1×768 .

Supervised via L teacher , a five-step reverse sampling process (N s = 5 realizations) followed by 64 × 64 → 512 × 512 upsampling synthesizes pseudo-label ensembles, yielding mean concentration targets cteacher and epistemic uncertainty variance U var .

(C) Fast Student Model: Ingests concatenated RGB-physics features X in = Concat[I RGB , C pinv ] ∈ R 5×512×512 through an initial convolution (F 0 ) and four parallel dilated residual branches (B 1 , B 2 , B 4 , B 8 with d ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}) to predict multi-head outputs O ∈ R 5×512×512 .

(D) Morphological Routing and Outputs: Aligns refined concentrations C mean (Head 1-2) and epistemic uncertainty U var (Head 3-4) via anchored hybrid distillation and physical RGB reconstruction (L student ), while a symmetric morphological routing module (Head 5 logits gated by chromatic envelope E DAB and Gaussian smoothing K smooth , 15 × 15, σ = 3.5) generates routing mask M attn to disentangle shared chromogens into Amyloid-β ( ŜAmyloid ), Tau ( ŜTau ), and Hematoxylin ( ŜHTX ).
